package_info.why_malicious: The 'everything' package is intentionally crafted to depend on every publicly available NPM package, resulting in a massive dependency tree. This causes denial of service (DoS) by exhausting storage space and breaking build processes for any project that installs it. The package is a form of dependency hell attack, weaponizing the package manager's dependency resolution mechanism to disrupt the NPM ecosystem.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package.json declares dependencies on every public NPM package, causing the package manager to recursively fetch and install millions of packages, leading to resource exhaustion and denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Declaring dependencies on every available package is highly abnormal and serves no legitimate development purpose. It is designed to overwhelm the package manager and system resources.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal package.json should only declare necessary dependencies. This package abuses the dependency mechanism to intentionally cause harm.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate package would ever depend on every public package; at most, meta-packages might aggregate a handful of related modules.
key_indicators: Dependencies list includes every public NPM package

attack_chain.action: User or CI/CD system installs the 'everything' package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers the NPM package manager to resolve and download all public packages.

attack_chain.action: NPM attempts to fetch and install millions of dependencies.
attack_chain.leads_to: System storage is exhausted, and build processes fail (Denial of Service).

behavioral_signatures: package.json with dependencies on an abnormally large number of packages
Install-time resource exhaustion (disk, memory) during dependency resolution
CI/CD build failures due to excessive dependency trees
file_indicators: package.json with thousands or millions of dependencies
Unusually large node_modules directory after install
network_indicators: Massive number of outbound requests to the NPM registry during install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose package.json declares dependencies on an unusually high number of other packages (e.g., more than 100). Flag and block installation of packages with dependency lists that include all or most public NPM packages. Alert on install-time resource exhaustion or excessive network requests to the NPM registry.
